targets.researchQuestion: Can current primary issuer evidence resolve the gating requirement for reproducible accelerator customer concentration and switching/share economics treatment?
targets.summary: Primary evidence materially improves the dossier but does not close the exact gate. AMD now discloses two separate multi-year agreements with OpenAI and Meta, each contemplating up to 6 GW of AMD data-center GPUs, and each accompanied by a warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares vesting against purchase milestones and other conditions. Q2 2026 Data Center revenue was $6.718B, up 107% year over year, with growth attributed primarily to EPYC and Instinct MI350 demand. However, AMD still does not quantify accelerator revenue by end customer, the share of Data Center revenue represented by either agreement/customer, or reproducible switching/share economics. The correct anti-stall disposition remains BLOCKED, not active indefinitely.

findings.fact: AMD Q2 2026 Data Center revenue was $6.718B and six-month Data Center revenue was $12.493B; Q2 Data Center operating income was $2.103B.

AMD disclosed multi-year OpenAI and Meta agreements under which each customer intends to deploy up to 6 GW of AMD data-center GPUs; AMD issued each customer a warrant for up to 160M common shares at $0.01 exercise price, vesting in tranches tied to Instinct GPU purchase milestones and specified stock-price/performance conditions. No tranche had vested as of June 27, 2026.

The warrant-linked structure is evidence of strategic customer concentration and customer-acquisition economics, but it cannot be converted into a customer revenue percentage or durable switching-cost/share metric without additional issuer/customer primary disclosure.

unknowns: Accelerator revenue attributable to OpenAI, Meta, or any other end customer is not quantified in the reviewed issuer filing.
No reproducible issuer-level metric was found for accelerator switching cost, workload migration friction, or customer share persistence.
falsifiers: A current AMD filing or primary customer filing that quantifies purchases/revenue by named accelerator supplier or customer would materially change this conclusion.
A contractual primary source disclosing minimum purchase commitments, termination economics, or supplier-share obligations would materially improve reproducibility.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: Search current OpenAI and Meta primary disclosures/contracts plus subsequent AMD 10-Q/10-K exhibits for minimum purchase commitments, named-customer revenue concentration, termination clauses, or supplier-share economics. Preserve future MI market-share persistence as non_gating_unknown rather than holding other names.

targets.researchQuestion: Can current primary evidence make customer concentration and overseas-fab capital-efficiency treatment reproducible enough for Chief review?
targets.summary: Yes. Primary issuer evidence now supplies a reproducible concentration record and a quantified overseas-fab margin/capital bridge. TSMC's 2025 Form 20-F reports its top ten customers at 78% of revenue, largest customer at 19%, and second-largest at 17%. Q2 2026 management reported $40.2B revenue, 67.7% gross margin, $15.7B quarterly capex, and explicitly quantified overseas-fab gross-margin dilution at 2-3 percentage points in early stages widening to 3-4 points later. The company also set 2026 capital budget at $52-56B and reported Arizona Fab 1 in high-volume production since Q4 2024, Fab 2 targeted for H2 2027 and Fab 3 construction underway. This closes the queue's stated concentration/capital-efficiency gate sufficiently for Chief reproducible factor/risk assembly; geopolitical timing remains a non-gating future uncertainty.

findings.fact: TSMC's ten largest customers represented approximately 78% of 2025 net revenue; the largest customer represented 19% and the second-largest 17%.

Q2 2026 revenue was $40.2B, gross margin 67.7%, operating margin 60.3%, and quarterly capex $15.7B. Management said overseas-fab ramp diluted gross margin and forecasts 2-3 percentage points of dilution in early stages widening to 3-4 points later.

TSMC stated a 2026 capital budget of $52-56B. Its 2025 annual report states Arizona Fab 1 entered high-volume production in Q4 2024, Fab 2 is expected to enter high-volume manufacturing in H2 2027, and Fab 3 construction began in 2025.

The disclosed customer percentages plus explicit overseas-fab margin dilution and capex budget are sufficient to encode concentration and capital-efficiency risk without guessing named-customer identities or future geopolitical outcomes.

unknowns: TSMC does not name the two largest customers in the cited concentration disclosure.
Future geopolitical disruption timing and ultimate subsidy realization remain uncertain.
nonGatingUnknowns: Exact future utilization by individual overseas fab beyond disclosed ramp milestones.
falsifiers: A later filing materially changing customer concentration or overseas-fab dilution guidance before Chief promotion should supersede these inputs.
Evidence that current overseas fabs are structurally excluded from the stated dilution guidance would invalidate the capital-efficiency bridge.

targets.researchQuestion: Can current primary issuer evidence encode China/export exposure and critical-supplier dependence as a reproducible factor/risk record?
targets.summary: Yes, for the queue's stated gate. ASML's Q2 2026 investor presentation gives current quarterly net-system-sales geography: China fell to 14% in Q2 from 19% in Q1 and 36% in Q4 2025. The 2025 annual report records China at 29.1% of total net sales for 2025 versus 36.1% in 2024 and explicitly states many components/subassemblies are single-sourced or supplied by a limited number of vendors, especially in EUV where multi-sourcing can be economically impractical. Current Q2 2026 results also raised full-year revenue guidance to €43-45B and gross margin to 54-56%, while export controls remain an identified risk. These are reproducible exposure/risk inputs. Exact future export-rule changes and supplier-specific outage probabilities are non-gating unknowns and should not hold promotion.

findings.fact: ASML Q2 2026 net system sales were €6.6B; ship-to geography was South Korea 43%, Taiwan 30%, China 14%, USA 9%, Japan 4%. Q1 2026 China was 19% and Q4 2025 China was 36%.
ASML's 2025 annual report states customers in China represented 29.1% of 2025 total net sales versus 36.1% in 2024.

ASML states many system components and subassemblies are single-sourced or supplied by a limited number of vendors; reliance is especially pronounced for EUV because complexity and uniqueness can make multi-sourcing economically impractical.
Q2 2026 total net sales were €9.326B with 54.0% gross margin; ASML raised 2026 total net sales guidance to €43-45B and gross margin to 54-56%.

Quarterly China ship-to mix plus annual total-sales exposure and explicit limited/single-source dependency are sufficient to encode current geographic/export and supplier-concentration risk without fabricating supplier-specific failure probabilities.

contradictions: Quarterly net-system-sales ship-to percentages are not identical in scope to annual total-net-sales geographic percentages; they must remain separately labeled rather than combined as one series.
unknowns: Supplier-specific revenue-at-risk or outage probabilities are not quantified in the reviewed public issuer sources.
Future export-control scope, licensing outcomes and timing remain uncertain.
nonGatingUnknowns: Future export-control rule changes and licensing timing.
Supplier-specific outage probability absent a disclosed quantitative issuer estimate.
falsifiers: A newer ASML filing or official restriction materially changing China exposure before Chief promotion should supersede the Q2/2025 figures.
Evidence that the annual-report supplier-risk language no longer applies to the current EUV supply chain would require re-underwriting.

systemRecommendation.summary: Shrink the blocker set: move TSM and ASML to Chief review; keep AMD binary-blocked on the exact unquantified customer/switching-economics gate. Do not spend Deep capacity on future geopolitical/export timing or future accelerator share persistence, which are explicit non-gating unknowns.
